title: List-dimension confinement (dim<=r-1) is the missing reverse bound for the n^2-monomial-line concentration
evidence: The claim is that the in-tree axiom-clean subspaceDesign_list_dim_bound (rank cap |L|<=|F|^{r-1} when tau(r)*n + r*n < (r+1)*a) supplies the 'missing reverse bound' for the n^2-monomial-line Poisson floor and thereby pins delta*. Probe scripts/probes/_407_conn/C061_design_reverse_bound.py (exact, prize regime mu=20..32, rho in {1/2,1/4,1/8,1/16}, q~n^4.5, eps*=2^-128, budget q*eps*~n, window-interior delta=1-rho-H(rho)/(beta log2 n)) shows the bound is VACUOUS across ALL prize parameters: the firing threshold rearranges to a/n > (rho+r)/(r+1), monotone increasing in r toward 1 (=unique decoding / near-capacity). The window-interior agreement is a/n = 1-delta = rho + H(rho)/(beta log n) ~ rho + o(1), only infinitesimally above rho; even r=1 demands a/n > (rho+1)/2 > rho, so NO r fires. Structural root (Q1): for PLAIN (unfolded, s=1) smooth-domain RS the subspace-design parameter is tau(r)=(k-1)/n ~ rho, CONSTANT in r, because a nonzero degree-<k polynomial has <=k-1 roots so any r-dim subspace of RS[k] fully vanishes on <=k-1 coordinates regardless of r. There is no tau(r)->0 decay; that decay is exactly what folding (s>1, FRS/GG25 subspace-design codes) buys, which the attack_plan itself concedes ('confinement needs tau(r)<1 (folding)'). The attack_plan's r=1 monomial-line instantiation needs tau(1) < 2(a/n)-1, which is NEGATIVE for rho<=1/4 (fails even with perfect folding tau(1)=0) and only ~0.014-0.022 at rho=1/2. Pushing r up to fire forces |F|^{r-1}=q^{r-1} >> budget n. This independently reproduces three already-recorded in-tree findings: (i) issue 407 Comment-1 rebuttal (line 400 of _issue407_full.md) -- concentration over the n^2-line family requires controlling tails to order ~log(n^2)=Theta(log n), i.e. deep moments E_r for r~log n = deep-moment validity = BGK; (ii) Comment 51 #3 (line 1422) -- the floor is EXTREME-VALUE not concentration, MDS line-average incidence ~ q^{-Theta(n/log n)} at the window interior, so worst/avg gap = q^{Theta(n/log n)} is unbridgeable by any Chernoff/union/concentration bound over n^2 lines; (iii) DISPROOF_LOG Loop16/Loop18 (lines 80, 819) -- subspace-design/folded-RS capacity machinery 'needs folded codes / subspace-design codes, NOT plain RS', and every first/second-moment/Johnson/pairwise-agreement argument bottoms out exactly at eta_0=sqrt(rho)-rho, the BOTTOM of the prize window, never the interior. The design bound is a Johnson/unique-decoding-side rank cap on the wrong side of the window; it is genuinely PROVEN (axiom-clean) but vacuous in the prize band for plain RS.
wall: W-Johnson (and underlying W-subspace/BGK): the design list-dim reverse bound is a pairwise/linear-algebraic Johnson-side cap whose firing threshold a/n > (rho+r)/(r+1) excludes the entire prize window interior for plain RS (tau(r)=rho constant, no folding decay); the genuine reverse bound for the n^2-line floor requires Theta(log n) deep moments = BGK/Paley square-root cancellation for thin mu_n.
honest_note: The connection's structural observation -- that 'list-dim confinement' and Comment-1's 'missing reverse bound' are about the same object (a rank/incidence cap below capacity) -- is genuinely insightful and CORRECT as a reframing, and subspaceDesign_list_dim_bound IS axiom-clean and proven. But the bound does not close or even reduce the prize: it is vacuous for plain smooth-domain RS at the window interior, because plain RS lacks the tau(r)->0 folding decay the bound needs (tau(r)=rho constant), and the firing region is the unique-decoding/near-capacity side (a/n->1), not the window interior (a/n~rho+o(1)). The attack_plan correctly identifies the gap ('needs tau(r)<1 (folding)') and that gap is fatal for the prize. Verdict OPEN (welds to W-Johnson and underneath to BGK), not REDUCED, because no strictly cleaner open statement is produced -- it restates the known fact that folding (subspace designs) buys what plain RS lacks. Numerics are exact integer/float prize-regime parameters (no full-group n=q-1 test); the tau(r)=rho claim for plain RS is a rigorous polynomial-root argument.
